title: JinkoSolar launches Tiger Neo 5.0, a 510 W rooftop panel for homes
lede: JinkoSolar's new all-black home panel reaches 25.5% efficiency and comes with a 40-year warranty. Here is the news in short.
bullets: New 48-cell, all-black panel (JKM485–510T series) for premium homes and villas with limited roof space.
Up to 510 W with 25.52% efficiency (about 255 W/m²).
New TAC cell technology combining TOPCon, heterojunction and back-contact designs.
Loses less power in the heat: −0.24%/°C, compared with about −0.26%/°C on earlier TOPCon panels.
Dual-glass, front side only; 1,762 × 1,134 × 30 mm and 22 kg.
40-year product warranty and 40-year linear power warranty.
Aimed first at Europe and Australia; price and availability not yet announced.
thailand_note: For Thai roofs the lower heat loss is worth about 0.8% more output on a hot day. Until a Thai price and local stock exist, our picks for small roofs stay the AIKO and LONGi back-contact panels; for large roofs 650 W panels remain the lowest cost per watt.

title: JinkoSolar stays the world's No. 1 solar panel maker for the 7th time
lede: JinkoSolar shipped 86.8 GW of panels in 2025 and kept the top spot again, but sales fell and the company made a loss. Here is the news in short.
bullets: 2025 shipments: 86.8 GW of solar modules, the world's No. 1 module seller for the seventh time.
All-time total: more than 400 GW shipped by the end of Q1 2026, over 220 GW of them Tiger Neo panels.
Current flagship: Tiger Neo 3.0 N-type TOPCon panels, over 24.8% efficiency and up to 670 W.
Patents: more than 3,500 by the end of 2025, including over 700 for N-type TOPCon technology.
2026 plan: panels above 640 W expected to be more than 60% of shipments.
The other side: shipments fell about 7% from 92.9 GW in 2024 and the company made a loss, citing weak prices, rising costs and industry overcapacity.
Outlook: 75–85 GW of panel shipments expected in 2026; energy storage grew 420% to 5.2 GWh in 2025.
thailand_note: pv magazine lists JinkoSolar itself as the author of the main article, so it is a company article rather than independent reporting. The decline and the loss come from TaiyangNews.

title: Harmony @Huailan: battery settings changed to buy less from the grid
lede: Our review of this Chiang Mai eco-lodge's 10 kW solar + battery system showed its battery settings were costing money. On 2 November 2026 we changed them remotely. Here is what changed, in plain words.
bullets: Before: the battery was held at 40% most of the day and night, and pushed up to 80% from 09:00 to 17:00.
Before: grid charging was on in every time slot, so the inverter bought grid power in the morning to fill the battery just before the sun could do it for free.
Now: the battery can run down to 25% in every time slot before the house draws from the grid.
Now: grid charging is off in every slot, so the battery is charged by the sun only. Time of Use stays on and selling to the grid stays off.
The inverter confirmed the new settings at 09:00 on 2 November 2026.
Expected result: less grid electricity bought, especially early in the morning, and more of the battery used every night.
Trade-off: in a night-time blackout there may be as little as 25% left in the battery; the owner can raise the night slots to 40% if backup matters more than savings.
thailand_note: Many hybrid systems in Thailand are left on installer default settings. Checking the battery and grid-charge settings against how the building actually uses power is a free way to cut the electricity bill.
